checks_run.procedure: Line-by-line review of every P1 mutation path for a server-side authorization check, validation, optimistic concurrency and an audit event: transformations/routes.ts, access/assignments.ts + policy.ts + rules.ts, organization/routes.ts, admin/routes.ts, identity/routes.ts + sessions.ts, platform/hooks.ts + idempotency.ts, access/denials.ts, audit/index.ts, migration 0003
checks_run.command: source review (Read) of the files named above
checks_run.expected: each mutation is authorized, validated, If-Match-guarded and audited in one transaction; reads are scope-filtered in SQL; sessions/CSRF sound
checks_run.actual: Transformation create/update/archive: requireRead then requireAction, If-Match (428/409) under a row lock, one audit event, outbox on create; lists use scopeFilter in SQL; the onSend guard fails closed when no policy decision was made. Assignments: self-grant refused, technical-admin approval SoD, revoke cascades derived grants under FOR SHARE/UPDATE. Sessions: 32-byte tokens hashed, HMAC CSRF + Origin on unsafe methods, rotation on login. Failed mutation authorization is audited. Exceptions found: F-DG1-140 (BU re-parent race), F-DG1-141 (destination parent not authorized), F-DG1-142 (rate-limit key). Not a defect: an Idempotency-Key replay returns the caller's stored original response without re-authorizing (same user, same key, 24 h).

summary: FAIL. Every required check ran: typecheck, build, lint, openapi:lint (33 ops), no-cdn, format, unit on Node 24 (325/325) and Node 22 (1 intermittent failure in 4 runs), integration twice on a disposable PostgreSQL 16 (200/200 each), gate/agent tooling (105/105), deploy tooling (59/59), installer offline ACs (13/14; AC-1 effect needs a registry, the D-057 residual), SBOM, historical DG0 validation, and the three ci.yml copies are identical. The review reproduced two mandatory-violation defects through the real API: concurrent business-unit re-parenting commits a hierarchy cycle (F-DG1-140, Medium) and re-parenting never authorizes the destination parent, so a unit-scoped manager can expose records to a sibling branch (F-DG1-141, Medium). Also a global rate-limit bypass (F-DG1-142, Medium) and four Low items (F-DG1-143 ajv lint bypass + test-only runtime deps; F-DG1-144 flaky web test; F-DG1-145 undocumented views; F-DG1-146 D-057 overstates 14/14 offline).
